purpose: Turn recurring YouTube/forum slot methods into machine-testable hypotheses without allowing creator anecdotes to become execution rules.

methods.claim: Play only a small fixed number of spins on a machine and move on if no quick win/taste appears.

sources.finding: Professor Slots links the 5-Spin Method as a recurring strategy.
Describes the method as a YouTube-born tactic: play up to five spins then move on if no win.
Documents the taste hypothesis but finds no demonstrated secret winning mechanism.

methods.math: Stopping after five spins limits exposure but cannot improve per-euro expectation on an IID fixed-math game.

methods.claim: Use a prescribed number of spins at one stake/denomination, then raise or change denomination to induce a hit/bonus.
examples: 15 spins for a win, 10 more after a win, then raise stake if no bonus

sources.finding: Search-indexed Eye of Horus Megaways method described 15 spins, 10 further after a win, then increased stake if no bonus.
Progressive betting appeared in five of 21 sampled slot-vlog videos; one creator changed denominations repeatedly while trying to make a game hit.

exceptionGate: verified persistent state separated by stake level

methods.claim: Always take another spin after a big hit so a second win is not missed.
methods.exceptionGate: Only retain if exact current rules document post-award persistent state or chained guaranteed feature.

methods.claim: Move to another machine/game after N losing spins because the current game is cold.
methods.salvage: Scanning other machines can be valid only when searching observable positive initial state such as MHB meters or persistent accumulators.

methods.claim: A guaranteed jackpot ceiling can create a calculable opportunity when current state is sufficiently favorable.

sources.finding: Current educational video explains MHB category and explicit guaranteed boundaries.
Analyzes target points using reset, ceiling, meter rise and trigger distribution.

methods.hardGuard: Do not assume uniform trigger distribution or creator thresholds for a Spanish title.

methods.claim: Visible state left by prior play may carry value into the next spin/session.

sources.finding: Ocean Magic is a variable-state game where favorable bubbles can create player advantage on suitable deployments.
Catalogs persistent-state mechanics such as bubbles/meters and separate bet-level states.

methods.hardGuard: Exact current Spanish online persistence and state scope must be independently proven.
